Does the app work on macOS or other platforms?
LastStats is developed and tested on Android. Behaviour on other platforms (macOS, Windows, Linux…) is unverified, bugs or unexpected behaviour may occur.
Yes! The source code is freely available on GitHub. The project is independent, built with passion by SanoBld. Feel free to contribute, report bugs, or leave a star ⭐.

With Last.fm, go to Settings > Account and enter your secret key (it is next to your API key at last.fm/api/accounts). With ListenBrainz, there is nothing more to add: your token is enough. Once connected, you can favorite tracks directly from the app.
How do levels and achievements work?

Your account level grows with your total scrobble count (there\'s no max level). Cards also get a border (bronze → iridescent) based on how many times that artist/track/album has been played. Everything is computed automatically from stats already cached locally, with no extra network calls.
How does power saving mode work?

Power saving mode reduces what the app does to save battery: tilt parallax is turned off, the screen refresh rate is capped at about 60 Hz, background updates run less often, and animated artwork and badge shine are paused. Images, exports and share cards keep full quality.\n\nYou can keep it always on, make it follow your phone\'s own battery saver, or have it turn on below a battery level you choose. You\'ll find it in Settings > Power saving mode.
How do I back up or restore my data?
Go to Settings > Backup. You can export a backup file (with or without your Last.fm key or ListenBrainz token) and import it later or on another device.
Yes, to some extent. Stats already loaded stay available offline thanks to local caching, but a connection is still needed to fetch new scrobbles.
Can I switch accounts or service?

Yes. From Settings > Account, sign out and sign in again with another username, or choose the other service (Last.fm or ListenBrainz) on the login screen. The local cache is reset automatically so that data is never mixed.
How do I set up notifications?
From Settings > Notifications, you can turn on an alert when a sync finishes, choose how often alerts appear, or turn notifications off completely if you prefer.
Artwork is missing or keeps loading. What can I do?

Clear the cache in the app (Settings > Cache), then in Android (Settings > Apps > LastStats > Storage > Clear cache). If images are still missing, back up your data (Settings > Backup), uninstall and reinstall the app, then restore your backup.

How do I get a Last.fm API key?

Sign in to Last.fm, open last.fm/api/account/create, enter an application name and a short description (the callback URL can stay empty), then copy the \"API key\" shown on last.fm/api/accounts. Enter it in LastStats together with your Last.fm username. The key belongs to you: LastStats has no shared key.

Last.fm announced that, from December 1, 2026, an API key only works while the Last.fm account that owns it has a Last.fm Pro subscription. Keys owned by free accounts stop working on that date. Only the owner of the key has to pay: your listening history and your account do not change. If you do not want to subscribe, you can use ListenBrainz instead, which is free.
What happens if my key stops working?

LastStats keeps showing the data already saved on your device, but new data can no longer be loaded and an error message is shown. Subscribe to Last.fm Pro (or enter a key owned by a Pro account) to make everything work again, or switch to ListenBrainz in Settings > Account.
How do my listens reach Last.fm?
LastStats only displays your scrobbles; it does not record any. Use a scrobbler app or a music player with Last.fm support (for example Pano Scrobbler on Android), signed in to your Last.fm account.
Why are my latest scrobbles missing?

First check that your scrobbler is working: the track must appear on your profile at last.fm. Then pull down to refresh LastStats. Last.fm limits how many requests an application can send, so LastStats spaces out its calls: a very large history can take a while to sync the first time.
Where do I find my ListenBrainz user token?

Sign in on listenbrainz.org, open listenbrainz.org/settings/ and copy the \"User token\". Keep it private: it identifies you. In LastStats, enter your ListenBrainz username (your MusicBrainz username) and the token. It stays on your device only.

Yes. ListenBrainz is an open-source project of the non-profit MetaBrainz Foundation, and it is free to use. LastStats only needs your user token: there is no API key to create. Your listens are public data released under the CC0 license.
Why are my statistics empty or missing?

ListenBrainz computes statistics on its own servers, so they can be late for a new account, after a large import or when the service is busy. In that case the API simply answers that nothing is ready yet. Your listens appear first and the statistics follow later. Please try again a little later.
How do I bring my Last.fm history to ListenBrainz?

Sign in on listenbrainz.org (a MusicBrainz account is required) and open listenbrainz.org/import-data/ to import your Last.fm listens. When many people import at the same time, it can take a while. When you switch service, LastStats also offers to transfer the scrobbles saved on your device.
How do I send my listens to ListenBrainz?

LastStats only displays your listens. To record them, use a player or scrobbler app compatible with ListenBrainz, signed in with your token; the list of supported apps is on listenbrainz.org. Remember that your listens are public.
